Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the quick kickoff yesterday. As we move toward approval for production, our Privacy & Security team has a few specific asks to complete Meridian's DPIA and procurement checklist:

- An extract of Redwood's Art. 30 processing register relevant to the Meridian account (sample CSV or ledger extract is fine)
- A short operational note describing how subprocessor activity is tracked (onboarding/offboarding events, notification cadence)
- KMS/wrap description and whether customer key wrap is supported for dedicated/private deployments
- Copies or links to SOC 2 and any relevant transfer/legal mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent)

We'd like to have the above by the end of next week (2027-04-02) to keep our timeline. I'm attaching our DPIA scope doc and the procurement checklist for context.

Attachments: Meridian_DPIA_Scope.pdf (pdf), Meridian_procurement_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Happy to hop on a short call — are you available tomorrow between 11–2 PT?

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-28T14:20:00Z
Subject: Art.30 extract and operational notes (pre-read)

Hi team,

Following up with the pre-read materials I mentioned — attached is a scoped Art.30 CSV extract for Meridian (redacted example rows), plus a brief operational note on subprocessors and transfer safeguards. Highlights below:

- Art.30 extract: columns include processing_activity_id, purpose, categories_of_data, recipients, subprocessor_name, subprocessors_role, transfer_basis, retention_period, controller_or_processor. The attached CSV (art30-register-20270328.csv) contains three representative rows scoped to typical Redwood inference flows.
- Subprocessor lifecycle: we maintain an onboarding ledger with event timestamps (requested_on, approved_on, notif_sent_on, contract_signed_on, status). Notifications to customers are automated for major changes; quarterly inventory snapshots are produced for audit requests.
- Transfers & safeguards: Redwood defaults to SCCs for EU->US transfers; for specific jurisdictions we provide documented transfer impact analyses. For Dedicated/Private there is an option for onshore-only hosting and customer key wrap. See kms-wrap-summary.pdf for supported KMS patterns.

Attachments: art30-register-20270328.csv (csv), kms-wrap-summary.pdf (pdf), dpia-evidence-index.csv (csv)

Notes on scope: the attached Art.30 extract is scoped to the processing activities Redwood performs as a processor for customer workloads (no customer-identifying payload data included). If Meridian needs a fuller ledger export or a signed attestation, let us know and we'll surface the appropriate request flow.

--
Karthik Iyer
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
